title: RightShip tanker vetting baseline criteria Revision 4.0 in force
summary: Rev 4.0 (dated 1 Oct 2026) rewrites the Oil, Gas & Chemical baseline. Revisions log: expanded vetting policy and Safety Score treatment; new 'unknown vessel attributes' rule; consolidated PSC rules (3+ detentions in 24 months = Unacceptable); Category A/B vs C/D incident review periods; refined age/CAP/SIRE-CDI/crew matrix/HVPQ rules (max age 25 tanker / 25 LPG / 35 LNG; CAP 2 with Level 2 FDA, 36-month validity; crew matrix ≤30 days; HVPQ ≤3 months).
short_title: RightShip baseline criteria Rev 4.0 now in force
headline: RightShip tightens tanker PSC, age, CAP and paperwork rules (Rev 4.0)
key_numbers: Max age 25 yrs tanker / 25 LPG / 35 LNG
changed: Rewritten baseline, dated 1 Oct 2026
New rule: unknown vessel attributes (e.g. class, flag, P&I, ownership) = Unacceptable until verified
PSC detention, deficiency and close-out rules consolidated
Incident review periods split: Category A/B vs C/D
what_to_do: Check each vessel's RightShip profile for unknown attributes and recent PSC detentions.

title: CDI announces AEPS questionnaire – new SIR chapters 15–24
summary: CDI's 'Alternative Energy & Power Supply' questionnaire adds chapters 15–24 to the 10th Edition Ship Inspection Report (biofuels, methanol/ethanol, ammonia, LPG and LNG as fuel, WAPS, onshore power, fuel cells, ShaPoLi/EPL, onboard carbon capture), with section/question renumbering. Official launch scheduled Monday 14 December 2026.
headline: CDI adds 10 alternative-fuel chapters to the SIR and renumbers questions
changed: New AEPS questionnaire: biofuels, methanol/ethanol, ammonia, LPG/LNG as fuel
Also WAPS, onshore power, fuel cells, ShaPoLi/EPL, onboard carbon capture
Section and question numbering will change
Applies to all vessel and inspection types CDI covers
what_to_do: Remap CDI question numbers in your pre-vetting checklists before 14 Dec 2026.

title: OCIMF launches revised SIRE Cat-1 inspector training
summary: First run in London 7–11 Sep 2026: a seven-week blended course (online asynchronous + face-to-face workshops) with staged assessments; 14 OCIMF member organisations attended.
short_title: Revised SIRE Cat-1 inspector training launched
headline: OCIMF runs its revised SIRE Cat-1 inspector course for the first time
changed: Online learning plus face-to-face workshops in London
Staged assessments for new inspectors

title: Revised information paper: Safety Critical Equipment and Spare Parts Guidance
summary: OCIMF published the revised paper (replaces the 2018 first edition): a risk-based approach to identifying, documenting and maintaining safety-critical equipment and spares within an ISM-aligned SMS. Relevant to SIRE 2.0 defect/PMS questions.
short_title: Revised Safety Critical Equipment & Spares guidance
headline: OCIMF updates its guidance on safety-critical equipment and spares
changed: Risk-based approach to identifying critical equipment and spares
Covers documenting and maintaining them within an ISM-aligned SMS
what_to_do: Compare your SMS critical-equipment and spares procedures with the revised paper.

title: MEG5: industry survey and MEG4 comment register open until 23 Oct 2026
summary: OCIMF is developing the 5th edition of the Mooring Equipment Guidelines and seeks practitioner feedback via a 20–30 minute survey and a MEG4 comment register; both close 23 October 2026.
headline: OCIMF asks practitioners to shape the next Mooring Equipment Guidelines (MEG5)
changed: Survey on the 5th edition of MEG
MEG4 comment register open in parallel
what_to_do: Send your mooring feedback through the survey before 23 Oct 2026.

title: OCIMF committee plans TMSA3 and MEG4 revisions and SIRE question-guidance updates
summary: The P&A Tankers, Barges & Terminal Interfaces committee (Houston, 17–18 Mar 2026) was briefed on a revised way of working for revising MEG4 and TMSA3, plans for the Programmes Modernisation Project and plans for revisions to SIRE question guidance. No publication dates announced.
short_title: TMSA3, MEG4 and SIRE guidance revisions planned
headline: TMSA3, MEG4 and SIRE question guidance are heading for revision
changed: Committee briefed on a new way of revising MEG4 and TMSA3
Plans to revise SIRE question guidance
Programmes Modernisation Project under way

title: PSC Concentrated Inspection Campaign on cargo securing (1 Sep – 30 Nov 2026)
summary: Joint CIC on loading, stowage and securing of cargo units and cargo transport units, applied alongside routine PSC inspections; one CIC inspection per ship per MoU. Limited relevance for tankers.
short_title: Paris & Tokyo MoU CIC on cargo securing
headline: Paris and Tokyo MoUs check cargo securing in a joint campaign
key_numbers: 1 CIC inspection per ship per MoU
changed: Focus: loading, stowage and securing of cargo units
Runs alongside routine PSC inspections
Limited relevance for tankers

title: SIRE 2.0 Focused Inspection Campaign on ship hardening (Q7.2.1)
summary: Started 1 Oct 2025 for a minimum of six months; inspectors address Q7.2.1 on every SIRE 2.0 inspection; interim review planned Feb 2026. A TANKEROperator article by OCIMF's Programmes Director (Apr/May 2026, third-party source) says the FIC concludes end of March 2026.
short_title: SIRE 2.0 focused campaign on ship hardening (Q7.2.1)
headline: SIRE 2.0 inspectors check ship hardening (Q7.2.1) on every inspection
changed: Q7.2.1 Ship hardening and access control asked on every SIRE 2.0 inspection
Checks crew familiarity with company hardening procedures and plans
A third-party article says the campaign ended March 2026
what_to_do: Review company procedures and ship-hardening plans, as OCIMF recommends.
